payload.text: screen-protocol-v1: Screen gate amended pre-results for daily-bar crypto: PASS requires >=40 trades AND net P&L > 0 after costs (SCHEMA v1 default >=100 was intraday-calibrated). Train fence: the screen receives only bars dated <= 2023-12-31; later data is gauntlet holdout. Costs from each spec's cost_model, both fields fractions of notional, applied per side. Execution: signals on close, fills next open; warmup enforced; same-bar stop+target resolves to stop; gaps fill at open; no leverage (notional capped at 1x equity); multi-asset = independent equal-capital books combined by mean. Engine: pipeline/engine.py at the commit carrying this note.

When the z-score is stretched in the direction implied by the surprise (red bars), we see significantly less reversion. For large surprises, the reversion is actually negative on average (that is, we see continuation – a manifestation of the post-earnings drift effect).

payload.claim: In a triangulated stat arb framework, aggregating (flattening) z-score signals across multiple overlapping equity pairs/spreads into ticker-level signals naturally produces a long/short portfolio where genuinely mispriced stocks are identified while noise from individual pair relationships washes out.

The simple act of aggregating votes across multiple spreads naturally tends to build a portfolio of mispriced stocks.
Stuff that’s genuinely mispriced shows up as mispriced against multiple partners. Noise tends to wash out. You end up long the things that are cheap across multiple relationships and short the things that are rich.

Same magnitude, opposite signs. One spread becomes two votes.

payload.claim: Trend-following effects are observed in the data across a range of crypto assets, consistent with crypto markets having hard-to-pin-down fair value and no obvious price anchor.
payload.quote: You tend to see trend effects in markets where fair value is hard to pin down and there’s no obvious anchor for what something should be worth. Crypto is a good example. If everyone forgot the Bitcoin price and we asked them what it should be, there’d be zero consensus. It’s fragmented, hard to value, heavily retail, traded with lots of leverage. The conditions for trend effects to persist appear to be in place. And we do see them in the data, across a bunch of crypto assets.

payload.text: gauntlet-protocol-v1: Five-gate battery on the 2024+ holdout, specs frozen at registration (no re-fitting, so walk-forward = one OOS pass; full-history run, trades attributed IS/OOS by entry_date vs 2023-12-31). Gates in fixed fail order: (a1) OOS net>0; (a2) per-trade edge decay > -25% vs IS (fail if IS edge <= 0); (b) 2000-path seeded IID bootstrap of pooled per-trade portfolio contributions (seed=int(strategy_id,16)%2^31), P05 terminal > 1.0 [amends SCHEMA's unfalsifiable 'P05 equity > 0' - equity cannot reach 0 under no-leverage sizing]; (c) ruin = path equity <= 0.5x start, P(ruin) < 5%; (d) deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 [amends vacuous 'DSR > 0'; DSR = PSR(E[max SR]) per Bailey-LdP, trials = sibling group size, variance across trials = sample variance of all group siblings' full-run daily Sharpes, higher-moment PSR corrections]; (e) OOS net > 0 at 2x slippage. Selection (pre-declared): one quarantine slot per sibling group = highest-DSR passer, tie -> lexicographically smallest strategy_id; other passers graveyarded as sibling_not_selected. Compounding convention: contribution = return_net x notional_frac, equity *= 1+c. Engine: pipeline/{engine,stats,gauntlet}.py at the commit carrying this note.

payload.text: gauntlet-protocol-v2: Supersedes v1 for all FUTURE verdicts; v1 verdicts stand and the 13 graveyarded gen-1 strategies stay buried (graveyard is terminal). WHY: v1's gate (a2) compared raw per-trade edge IS vs OOS with no volatility normalization, so a shrinking opportunity set scored identically to strategy decay. Over this fence passive buy-and-hold decayed -66% (BTC) and -122% (ETH) while the 13 strategies decayed -56% to -73%, i.e. less than the market did; the gate could not tell the two apart. This flaw was identified FROM gen-1's results, and is corrected here BEFORE any gen-2 spec exists. CHANGE: gate (a2) now compares volatility-normalized per-trade edge (edge / annualized realized vol of the traded universe measured over that window's bars), same -25% threshold, same fixed fail order; verdicts additionally record is_edge_raw, oos_edge_raw, is_vol, oos_vol so the v1 number is recomputable from any v2 verdict. CHANGE: DSR trials = every strategy_registered entry in the chain (not the sibling group), variance across all their full-run daily Sharpes - the honest multiple-testing count, which rises as we search more. COMPOSER: composition fingerprints (universe + blocks + params, excluding identity fields) block re-registration of any previously registered composition in any state, including duplicate siblings within one family, so no strategy returns under a fresh id. LIMITATION DISCLOSED: the 2024+ holdout is no longer virgin - gen-1 consumed it once and gen-2 is designed knowing what that showed; cumulative trial counting is a partial mitigation, not a cure. RATCHET: diagnose_protocol_v2.py may be run only after this note is chained; its result may TIGHTEN this protocol, never loosen it, and any change requires a new pre-declared note. Engine: pipeline/{engine,stats,composer,gauntlet}.py at the commit carrying this note.

gauntlet-protocol-v2 diagnostic result (ratchet check, run after the v2 note was chained; see docs/diagnostics/2026-08-15-v1-under-v2.txt): 0 of 22 graveyarded gen-1 strategies would pass under v2. The gate did NOT lose its teeth, so no tightening is triggered and gen-2 proceeds under v2 as chained. Detail worth recording: v2 is not merely a relabelling - it is strictly HARSHER in aggregate. Vol normalization materially moved the decay numbers (the 12 trend_scan siblings improve from -56/-73% raw to -34.7/-56.1% normalized, and 4 breakout siblings move to POSITIVE normalized decay of +28.6/-19.3%), i.e. much of what v1 scored as strategy decay really was the opportunity set shrinking. But those 4 then fail the DSR gate instead (0.220-0.443 vs the 0.95 floor), because trials_n=22 with variance taken across all 22 strategies' full-run Sharpes raises E[max SR] far above the old per-sibling-group hurdle, under which every gen-1 DSR read >=0.99. Net effect: both amendments bite, in opposite directions, and nothing survives. Note that trials_n grows as more strategies are registered, so the DSR hurdle rises further for generation 2 and beyond. The 22 stay buried; graveyard is terminal.

payload.text: gauntlet-protocol-v3: Supersedes v2 for all FUTURE verdicts. v1 and v2 verdicts stand. All 56 previously registered strategies remain in graveyard, which is terminal; the composition-fingerprint guard still blocks re-registration of any of them; the lifecycle state machine is UNCHANGED - no new transitions, nothing resurrected, no amendment to terminal states. WHY: v2 gated entry to PAPER trading on a deflated Sharpe of at least 0.95, where SR* = sqrt(V[SR]) x multiplier(N) and V[SR] was the sample variance of our own registered strategies' observed Sharpes. Measured on this registry at N=56 the implied hurdle was 1.86 annualized against a best-ever-achieved 1.42. The driver is sqrt(V[SR])=0.80, the spread of our own results (-1.36 to +1.42): with only the best 30 registered the hurdle would have been 0.40. Honestly registering failures is what made the gate unpassable, and a rule that punishes transparency is mis-specified. The gauntlet's job is to identify strategies that are robust, positive expected value and slow to decay; its other five gates test exactly that. CHANGE 1: the DSR check is REMOVED from the gauntlet stage. The five robustness gates are unchanged in threshold and in fixed fail order: OOS net > 0, volatility-normalized edge decay > -25%, Monte Carlo P05 terminal > 1.0, P(ruin) < 5%, 2x-slippage OOS net > 0. Deflated Sharpe is STILL computed and STILL recorded in every verdict's metrics - informational at this stage - and still selects the one strategy per sibling group that takes the quarantine slot, ranked DSR descending with ties broken by the lexicographically smallest strategy_id. It is computed against EFFECTIVELY INDEPENDENT trials via the deterministic, order-independent clustering in pipeline/cluster.py; verdicts record both trials_n (= cluster count k) and registered_n (raw count), and artifact config.json carries the full cluster assignment. CHANGE 2: the DSR test MOVES to the quarantine -> live gate. Threshold DSR >= 0.95 UNCHANGED. It will be computed on the QUARANTINE FORWARD RECORD only, with N = the number of strategies that have entered quarantine to date and V[SR] the variance across those strategies' quarantine Sharpes. THIS GATE CANNOT BIND FOR AT LEAST 60 TRADING DAYS, its final calibration is not chosen here, and THIS NOTE DOES NOT AUTHORISE ANY LIVE TRANSITION - the live gate is pre-declared in its own note before any strategy approaches it. CHANGE 3: quarantine becomes a real daily forward test. python -m pipeline.quarantine --date YYYY-MM-DD appends one quarantine_decision per quarantined strategy per asset per trading day: {strategy_id, date, asset, action, price, position_frac, equity}, computed from bars up to and including that date only, refusing any date with no bar, idempotent on (strategy_id, date, asset) so a missed day is backfillable, with equity rebased to 1.0 at the strategy's quarantine entry date. Each date's rows are preceded by one quarantine_data_snapshot {date, data_sha256:{asset:hex}, bars_sha256:{asset:hex}} recording the price data those decisions were computed from: data_sha256 is the whole CSV, as screen.py and gauntlet.py already record it, and bars_sha256 covers the header plus every row dated at or before that date, LF-normalized. The runner recomputes each book from the first bar every day, so re-running a date whose bars_sha256 no longer matches is REFUSED rather than silently recomputed against different bars; a refresh that only appends later bars changes data_sha256 but not bars_sha256 and is correctly a non-event, which is what keeps a missed day backfillable. Pre-declared graduation criterion, MECHANICAL PART: at least 60 trading days accrued, counted once per date rather than once per asset. The P25-P75 cone recorded by the gauntlet is NOT applied at this gate and is NOT a pass/fail criterion. It is a terminal-equity distribution over a strategy's FULL trade count, so a 60-day forward record producing a handful of trades is not comparable to it, and treating it as a threshold would be unsound. --review therefore reports days accrued against the 60-day minimum, prints the stored cone as information, and states in its own output that the two are not comparable. The quantitative graduation comparison belongs to the quarantine -> live gate, is pre-declared in its own chained note before any strategy approaches it, and cannot bind for at least 60 trading days. The --review command reports progress and WRITES NOTHING; graduation is a separately human-gated decision. CHANGE 4: the composition-fingerprint guard becomes SIBLING-level. A sibling whose composition was previously registered in any state is dropped individually and its family survives with the remainder; a family whose siblings ALL collide is dropped entirely; intra-family duplicate siblings still drop the whole family as a malformed proposal. Exact compositions remain PERMANENTLY unregisterable, so a buried idea can only return at different parameters - if only the exact buried point worked, it was overfit. THIS CHANGE LOOSENS THE GAUNTLET STAGE and was identified from generation 2's results; it is declared here BEFORE any generation 3 spec exists. Block grammar, screen protocol, training fence and honesty guard are all UNCHANGED. LIMITATION: the 2024+ holdout has now been consumed twice, and removing the DSR gate mitigates repeated search less than v2 did at this stage - that protection now sits at quarantine, which is stronger evidence but arrives later. Engine: pipeline/{engine,stats,cluster,composer,gauntlet,quarantine}.py at the commit carrying this note.

payload.text:
gauntlet-protocol-v4: Supersedes v3 for all FUTURE verdicts. v1, v2 and v3 verdicts stand. All 77 previously graveyarded strategies remain buried, which is terminal; the composition-fingerprint guard still blocks re-registration of any of them; the lifecycle state machine is UNCHANGED - no new transitions, nothing resurrected, no amendment to terminal states. Pre-declared before any strategy has been evaluated under it and before any generation-4 specification exists.

WHY: the research layer and the trading-systems pipeline judged candidates by different standards, so a candidate's fate depended on which pipeline found it. This note makes one standard, so that a claim about several systems clearing one bar can be made honestly rather than requiring an explanation of which bar each one cleared. Direction of travel is one way: the research layer adopts the SOP's standard, and the SOP's gates do not move.

GATES RETAINED FROM v3, UNCHANGED: oos_negative, edge_decay, mc_p05, p_ruin, cost_stress. The deflated Sharpe is still computed and recorded. Under v3 it stopped gating this stage, moving to the quarantine-to-live gate where forward evidence exists to compute it on. Under v4 it also stops ranking siblings. It now influences no decision at this stage.

GATE ADDED - sharpe_floor: train-window annualized Sharpe below 0.4 is an auto-reject regardless of every other gate, taken from the SOP where a backtested Sharpe under 0.4 is presumptively false. This gate is knowingly non-binding today and that is stated here rather than discovered later: every one of the 43 strategies that has ever reached the gauntlet scored at least 0.577 on the train window, and all 24 specifications below 0.4 had already died at the screen. It is adopted because it makes the two pipelines textually identical and because it will bind if the screen is ever loosened.

GATE ADDED - pbo: probability of backtest overfitting by CSCV, S=16, all 12870 splits. Pass is below 0.20. Between 0.20 and 0.50 fails the configuration. Above 0.50 means the selection process is actively harmful and kills the entire sibling group on that universe rather than the single configuration, which is the SOP's rule adopted verbatim. Two properties of how it is computed here. It runs on the TRAIN WINDOW ONLY: the 2024-onward holdout has already been consumed three times and this protocol does not consume it a fourth. And EVERY sibling enters the matrix, including those that died at the screen, because computing PBO over survivors only would filter the matrix on performance and understate overfitting, which defeats the gate. When a family is killed, each member's recorded reason remains its own first failure in gate order and the family kill is recorded as a separate flag on every member; a strategy that independently failed oos_negative is not relabelled as a PBO casualty, because the chain would otherwise permanently hide that it was separately broken.

GATE ADDED - plateau: neighbourhood selection replacing point-winner selection. This is the gate this protocol exists for. The SOP forbids selecting the best single configuration and requires selection by neighbourhood quality, on the reasoning that a lone peak surrounded by cliffs is the signature of overfitting rather than of edge. A candidate qualifies only if all of the following hold. (1) Its family has at least one swept dense axis; a family with none fails with no_swept_axis, because without a neighbourhood there is no robustness evidence and every other clause would pass vacuously. (2) Every swept axis has a registered sibling one step BELOW and one step ABOVE it; failing this is edge_of_grid, because a candidate at the boundary of a grid, or one whose neighbouring grid point was never registered as a sibling, has never been perturbed in that direction and cannot claim a plateau from there. (3) The candidate and every one of its one-step neighbours score at least 90 percent of the family's best score. (4) No neighbour died at the screen on trade_count, because turnover is a structural property of a configuration rather than a noisy metric and a 24-trade sibling can post a flattering per-trade Sharpe while being untradeable. Among qualifying candidates that passed every other gate, the winner is the one whose WORST score across itself and its neighbours is highest, ties breaking on the lexicographically smallest strategy id. The selection function reads no point metric of any kind. The single objective throughout is the train-window annualized Sharpe, computed identically for every sibling regardless of its screen or gauntlet outcome.

CONSEQUENCES OF THE PLATEAU RULE, ACCEPTED DELIBERATELY: a two-value sweep can never produce a survivor because both points are grid edges, and on a three-value sweep only the middle point is eligible. The Composer's validator therefore enforces that every swept axis carries at least THREE values and that those values are CONTIGUOUS on the parameter's declared grid. Contiguity is not a convenience. Neighbours are defined against the declared grammar grid, so a family sweeping 20, 55 and 100 out of a grid of 20, 35, 55, 75, 100 would satisfy the three-value rule and still yield nothing, because the middle point's real neighbours at 35 and 75 were never registered. The alternative, defining neighbours against whichever values a family happened to sweep, was rejected: it would make a 20-to-55 jump count as a one-step perturbation, which is precisely the coarse-grid problem the dense block types were introduced to eliminate.

RECORDED, NOT GATED, matching the SOP which reports rather than gates these; each records which window it was computed on so no reader has to infer it. Harvey-Liu multiple-testing haircut, nonlinear, on the train window, using Bonferroni, the most conservative of the three adjustments Harvey and Liu give; because the number is reported rather than gating, conservatism costs nothing. Purged walk-forward, three folds on the train window, purge gap 200 bars which is at least the grammar's longest lookback, reported as fold results plus the SOP's two summary flags. Regime-conditional split on the out-of-sample window under one ruler declared for the whole protocol: BTC close against its 200-day moving average with a 5 percent band around the average counted as chop rather than weak trend.

A DECLARED DIVERGENCE: the SOP's Phase 5 checklist treats purged walk-forward majority pass and catastrophic veto as binding on designation. Here they are recorded and do not gate. This is stated as a difference rather than presented as equivalence. Promoting them to gates is a one-line change and would be a tightening, permitted freely by the ratchet.

RATCHET POSITION: this protocol only tightens. Three gates are added, none is removed, no threshold is loosened, and every v3 gate is retained unchanged, so v4 is a strict superset and no buried strategy can newly pass under it. That is a structural fact rather than a statistical one, which means the ratchet cannot be tripped by this protocol. It therefore carries none of the evidence-and-argument burden that v3 had to discharge when it relocated the deflated Sharpe. The standing rule is unchanged: a future protocol may tighten freely, and any loosening requires the evidence and the argument on this chain before the results it would affect exist.

THE ADDED GATES BITE RATHER THAN DECORATE, measured by a write-free diagnostic run before this note was chained. Of the 12 sibling groups on the chain, CSCV would family-kill 3 at PBO 0.902, 0.824 and 0.629, and fail 3 more at 0.451, 0.449 and 0.342, leaving 6 passing. The PBO gate alone would therefore have eliminated half the families ever registered. Twenty-four of the 80 registered strategies would fail the Sharpe floor, all 24 of them already dead at the screen.

RETROACTIVITY: this standard does not apply to the three strategies already in quarantine, which keep their v3 verdicts. That was decided and chained separately, before this protocol existed, as the quarantine-standard-asymmetry note at registry entry 2308, commit 1b5da5e. It is cross-referenced here rather than restated, because it was deliberately pre-declared before the successor standard existed so that the exemption could not have been chosen after seeing whom it helps. What that exemption costs can now be measured: under this protocol's PBO gate, 9b6753a48c4d0ccd in family channel_breakout_both_fixedfrac would FAIL at 0.342, while ad654fd8097717bd at 0.184 and ef7712f41e2188e2 at 0.118 would pass. One of the three would not have reached quarantine under the standard now being declared. It keeps its place. This is recorded to make the cost of the exemption legible, not to reopen it; reopening it would be exactly the retroactive re-judging that the exemption, and the rule keeping 77 strategies buried, both exist to forbid. Quarantine's forward record remains the leveller, since after 60 trading days all three are assessed on identical forward evidence.

WHAT IS KNOWINGLY NOT CORRECTED: the Composer's prior-knowledge leakage is real, unmeasured, and uncorrectable by the deflated Sharpe at any value of N. The model that proposes strategy families has read the literature on this asset class, so its priors already encode which strategies historically worked on this data. N counts configurations whose performance was actually observed, clustered to effective trials. Inflating it to account for the model's internal search would look like a correction while correcting nothing, because a configuration the model considered and discarded was never backtested and so never inflated any observed maximum. This is declared as a permanent limitation of the pipeline rather than priced into a number. Separately, the drift between the batch approved at the dry-run gate and the batch actually registered is now logged; it is mechanically observable and was previously lost. It is not a multiple-testing trial count, for the reason just given, and is recorded as provenance rather than as a denominator.

DIFFERENCES FROM THE SOP THAT SURVIVE, argued rather than smoothed over. First, the stage at which the deflated Sharpe is applied: both pipelines use 0.95, but trading-systems applies it at designation against a known search burden of N=1737 while the research layer applies it at the quarantine-to-live gate on the forward record, each where the evidence to compute it honestly exists. Second, deflation of N: trading-systems uses the raw trial count, the research layer clusters to effectively independent trials; this is defensible but it is a real difference in the denominator and is named here rather than hidden inside a shared threshold. Third, the sample-size floor: the SOP requires that under roughly 100 trades the shortfall is declared and every gate tightened, while the research layer's screen admits at 40 trades; this gap was previously undeclared.

STATED BEFORE ANY RESULT EXISTS: adding gates raises the probability that generation 4 produces no survivors. Generation 3 was the first to produce any, and this standard is strictly harsher than the one that produced them. A ZERO-SURVIVOR GENERATION 4 IS AN ACCEPTABLE OUTCOME. Furthermore, three of these rules have never been exercised against real data: the plateau ratio of 0.9, the both-sides neighbour requirement, and the 0.20 PBO threshold are uncalibrated, and the write-free ratchet diagnostic cannot calibrate them, because no strategy currently on the chain uses a dense block type and so no existing family has a swept axis for the plateau rule to act on. The diagnostic can exercise the Sharpe floor and PBO against history and nothing else. That is a real gap in the evidence behind this protocol and it is recorded here rather than discovered later. PRE-COMMITTED CONSEQUENCE: if generation 4 produces no survivors, a per-gate breakdown of what died where will be published on this chain BEFORE any threshold is discussed or any successor protocol is drafted. The purpose is to make a zero informative, so that it is possible to tell whether the gates caught something real or whether a threshold was simply set too high, and so that the determination is made from the published breakdown rather than from whichever answer would be more convenient once the numbers are known.

payload.text:
generation-4 per-gate breakdown: PUBLISHED BEFORE ANY THRESHOLD IS DISCUSSED AND BEFORE ANY SUCCESSOR PROTOCOL IS DRAFTED. The gauntlet-protocol-v4 note pre-committed that if generation 4 produced no survivors, a per-gate breakdown of what died where would be published on this chain first, so that the determination of whether the gates caught something real or a threshold was simply set too high would be made from the published evidence rather than from whichever answer turned out to be convenient once the numbers were known. Generation 4 produced no survivors. This note discharges that promise. It reports what died where and states what the evidence does and does not establish. It proposes no threshold change and drafts no successor protocol.

THE FUNNEL. 30 specifications registered in 6 sibling groups under run id 2026-08-19-gen4, each group sweeping exactly one dense axis at all five contiguous values of that axis. 11 died at the screen: 10 on trade_count and 1 on net_negative. 19 reached the gauntlet. 19 failed. 0 reached quarantine, and 0 were recorded as sibling_not_selected, because no specification survived to the selection stage.

DEATHS BY GATE, in the protocol's own FAIL_ORDER. sharpe_floor 9. oos_negative 0. edge_decay 0. mc_p05 0. p_ruin 1. cost_stress 0. pbo 9. plateau 0. Adding the screen: trade_count 10 and net_negative 1. Total 30, which is every specification registered this generation.

PER FAMILY. symmetric_tstat_trend_ff, sweeping trend_scan_dense.max_lookback over 60 to 120: all 5 passed the screen, all 5 reached the gauntlet, all 5 failed on pbo at a group value of 0.689, train-window annualized Sharpe 0.845 to 1.236. symmetric_tstat_trend_voltarget, the matched sizing control arm sweeping the same axis at the same values: all 5 passed the screen, 4 failed on pbo at a group value of 0.803 and 1 failed earlier on p_ruin at 0.061 against a maximum of 0.05, train Sharpe 0.804 to 1.168. short_only_fast_macross_high_n, sweeping atr_stop_dense.mult over 1.5 to 3.5: 1 died at the screen on net_negative, 4 reached the gauntlet and all 4 failed on sharpe_floor with train Sharpe 0.122 to 0.209. below_ma_short_regime_trend, sweeping regime_ma_short_dense.ma_len over 50 to 250: all 5 passed the screen and all 5 failed on sharpe_floor with train Sharpe 0.043 to 0.204. symmetric_macross_stop_geometry, sweeping atr_stop_dense.mult: all 5 died at the screen on trade_count with 31, 34, 36, 38 and 38 trades against a floor of 40. breakout_vol_state_filter, sweeping vol_percentile_dense.max_pctile over 0.6 to 1.0: all 5 died at the screen on trade_count with 7, 7, 7, 7 and 11 trades.

PBO BY SIBLING GROUP, computed by CSCV at S=16 over all 12870 splits on the train window with every sibling in the matrix including screen deaths, exactly as the protocol specifies. symmetric_tstat_trend_ff 0.689. symmetric_tstat_trend_voltarget 0.803. symmetric_macross_stop_geometry 0.761. short_only_fast_macross_high_n 0.651. below_ma_short_regime_trend 0.873. breakout_vol_state_filter 0.030. Five of the six exceed the 0.50 family-kill line and every member of those five carries the pbo_family_kill flag. The one group PBO would have cleared, at 0.030, is the group whose every member had already died at the screen on trade count. The historical group values recomputed in the same run reproduce the write-free diagnostic reported in the protocol-v4 note exactly, including the three kills at 0.902, 0.824 and 0.629 and the quarantined pair at 0.342 and 0.118, which is evidence that the CSCV implementation used for these verdicts is the one the protocol was declared against.

FINDING 1: THE ZERO IS THE PBO GATE, AND IT IS NOT A NARROW MISS. Six gates precede pbo in FAIL_ORDER, so a specification recorded as failing pbo passed all six, and those six include every gate protocol-v3 had. The 9 specifications that died on pbo therefore satisfied the entire protocol-v3 battery: positive out-of-sample edge, edge decay within tolerance with eight of the nine improving out of sample rather than decaying and the ninth at negative 20.5 percent, Monte Carlo P05 between 1.30 and 5.32 against a floor of 1.0, probability of ruin between 0.000 and 0.036 against a maximum of 0.05, and positive net profit under the cost stress. Their deflated Sharpe values, which protocol-v3 used to rank siblings, run from 0.808 to 0.983. Under protocol-v3 all 9 would have passed the gauntlet and its one-slot-per-group selection would have sent two of them to quarantine: b476048b2df2ab6e at a deflated Sharpe of 0.983 and 0022247749b387eb at 0.978. They died instead at group PBO values of 0.689 and 0.803 against a pass line of 0.20 and a family-kill line of 0.50. That is not a threshold set marginally too high. It is a gate reporting that selection among those siblings is worse than a coin flip at picking the configuration that performs out of sample.

FINDING 2: THE SHARPE FLOOR BOUND, AND THIS PROTOCOL PREDICTED IT WOULD NOT. The protocol-v4 note adopted sharpe_floor while stating it was knowingly non-binding, reasoning that all 43 strategies that had ever reached the gauntlet scored at least 0.577 on the train window and that all 24 sub-0.4 specifications had already died at the screen. That prediction was wrong on the first generation judged under it: 9 of the 19 gauntlet-reachers had train Sharpe between 0.043 and 0.209, and the floor rather than the screen is what stopped them. The mechanism is visible and is not a defect in either gate. The screen admits on trade count and net profit and selects for neither Sharpe nor any ratio of return to variability, and generation 4 was the first generation to contain families designed explicitly to maximise trade count. short_only_fast_macross_high_n was proposed to attack the sample-size failure that killed generation 2's short family, and it succeeded at exactly that, clearing the 40-trade floor with 49 trades at a Sharpe of 0.13. The floor was adopted for textual parity between two pipelines and turned out to be the gate that catches a frequency-optimised family. The note also stated that this gate would bite if the screen were ever loosened. What actually happened is that the screen did not move and the population moved instead.

FINDING 3: THE PLATEAU RULE STILL HAS NO EVIDENCE. plateau is last in FAIL_ORDER and no specification reached it, so the gate this protocol exists for did not fire once, and select_survivors ran over an empty set. The protocol-v4 note recorded as a known gap that the plateau ratio of 0.9, the both-sides neighbour requirement and the 0.20 PBO threshold were uncalibrated, and that the write-free ratchet diagnostic could not calibrate them because no strategy then on the chain used a dense block type. Generation 4 closed part of that gap and not the part that was expected. It produced real evidence on sharpe_floor and on PBO and none whatsoever on the plateau rule. The geometry was in place for it: all six groups swept a dense axis at five contiguous values, which under the both-sides rule leaves the three interior points of each group eligible, 18 of the 30 registered specifications in total. Every one of those 18 was eliminated by an earlier gate. The plateau rule remains untested against real data after the generation that was meant to test it.

WHAT THIS BREAKDOWN DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It does not establish that the 9 pbo deaths were false discoveries, only that CSCV over their own sibling matrices reports that selection among them does not generalise; PBO is a statement about a selection procedure applied to a family, not a verdict on any single configuration's economics. It does not establish that 0.20 and 0.50 are the right lines, because a generation whose observed group values are 0.030, 0.651, 0.689, 0.761, 0.803 and 0.873 contains no observation anywhere near either line and therefore carries almost no information about where either line should sit. It does not establish anything about the plateau rule, for the reason given above. And it does not establish that generation 4's families were poor material: two of them held train Sharpe above 0.8 with out-of-sample edge intact, which is the strongest raw material this pipeline has produced, and they were rejected by a gate measuring a different property than the gates that admired them.

ALSO RECORDED, as provenance rather than as findings. The batch-gate drift for this generation was total. The batch approved at the dry-run gate was 49 specifications in 6 families and the batch chained by the real run was 30 specifications in 6 entirely different families, with no family name in common. Generation 3's drift was 20 to 24 with families surviving. Both figures are in logs/batch_drift.jsonl. The dry-run gate is therefore a check on whether the Composer is producing sane families and is not a gate on specific specifications, and it cannot be one while the real run issues a fresh non-deterministic call. Separately, the screen metric net_pnl is final combined equity less one and marks an open position to market at the fence, while the trades and win_rate metrics count closed trades only. breakout_vol_state_filter reported a 0.00 win rate alongside a net_pnl of +1.017 for that reason: 7 closed losing trades, and one position opened after 2020-09-03 that never closed. It changed no verdict this generation, because those specifications failed trade_count first and because every other specification's open-position contribution lay between 0.000 and negative 0.041. It is recorded here because a public net profit figure that can include unrealised marks should not have to be inferred from the code.

THE RATCHET IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOT BEING TESTED BY THIS NOTE. protocol-v4 may be tightened freely. Any loosening requires the evidence and the argument on this chain before the results it would affect exist, and the results generation 4 would affect now exist. This note is the evidence half of that requirement and deliberately contains no argument, because the promise was that the breakdown would be published before any threshold was discussed, and a breakdown that arrived carrying a proposal would not have been that.

pbo-validity-evidence: EVIDENCE PUBLISHED UNDER THE RATCHET, BEFORE ANY CHANGE TAKES EFFECT AND BEFORE THE RESULTS IT WOULD AFFECT EXIST. The gauntlet-protocol-v4 note's standing rule is that a future protocol may tighten freely and any loosening requires the evidence and the argument on this chain before the results it would affect exist. This note is that evidence, for a change to the pbo gate that would run in the permissive direction. It reopens nothing. Generation 4's 19 gauntlet failures and the 88 strategies buried before them stay buried, on the same principle that kept generations 1 through 3 buried when their protocols were superseded, and the three strategies in quarantine keep their protocol-v3 verdicts under the quarantine-standard-asymmetry note. Every measurement below was produced by a write-free diagnostic reading committed artifacts and this chain, changing no gate and no threshold.

THE DEFECT, WHICH IS ANALYTIC RATHER THAN STATISTICAL. The CSCV implementation computes omega as the out-of-sample rank of the in-sample winner divided by n_configs plus one, and counts a split as overfit when omega is less than or equal to 0.5. That is Bailey, Borwein and Lopez de Prado's own convention and the code documents it as such: the median out-of-sample rank counts as overfit rather than as a pass. The convention is harmless at the family sizes that literature assumes, where the boundary case has vanishing measure. At small ODD n_configs it is not harmless, because the median rank lands exactly on omega equals 0.5 and is swept into the overfit count. Under the idealised null in which the winner's out-of-sample rank is uniform, the expected pbo is therefore 0.5 exactly when n_configs is even, and n_configs plus one over two n_configs when it is odd. For a family of 5 that is 0.600. For a family of 3 it is 0.667. For 25 it is 0.520. The protocol's family-kill line is 0.50. At a family of 5 the no-skill expectation therefore sits ABOVE the line at which this protocol declares that the selection process is actively harmful.

WHICH FAMILIES THIS TOUCHES, AUDITED ACROSS EVERY SIBLING GROUP ON THE CHAIN. There are 18 sibling groups. The 12 registered before generation 4 have sizes 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6, 6, 8, 8, 8, 12 and 12. Every one is EVEN, so every one carries a uniform-rank null of exactly 0.500 and none is affected by the parity defect. All 6 generation-4 groups have exactly 5 members, so every one carries a null of 0.600. Generation 4 is the first generation in this pipeline's history to land on an odd family size, and it did so on every family it produced.

THE CAUSE IS INTERNAL TO PROTOCOL-V4 AND IS A COLLISION BETWEEN ITS TWO NEW GATES. The plateau gate requires a registered sibling one step below and one step above a candidate on every swept axis, so a three-value sweep leaves only its middle point eligible and a five-value sweep leaves three. The Composer's system prompt encodes exactly that reasoning, instructing it to prefer one or two well-motivated axes at FIVE contiguous values because five values leave three eligible candidates where three leave one. Five is odd. The plateau rule therefore drove every generation-4 family onto the single arm of the pbo estimator where that estimator is biased upward, and the bias is large enough to cross the pbo gate's own kill threshold. The two gates added by the same protocol are in mechanical conflict, and nothing in the protocol's design or in its write-free ratchet diagnostic could have surfaced it, because the diagnostic ran only against the pre-existing even-sized families.

THE MEASURED NULL, ON REAL DATA. The idealised uniform-rank calculation above assumes away the real return distribution, the correlation between siblings and the conditioning induced by splitting one fixed series into halves. To measure the null without assuming any of that, a PERMUTATION null was constructed directly from the committed generation-4 equity curves: for each day, the sibling labels are randomly permuted. The daily cross-section is preserved exactly, so the real fat tails, the real common market factor and the real cross-sectional dispersion all survive, and only PERSISTENT sibling-specific skill is destroyed. That is precisely the null the pbo gate's semantics assume. Measured pairwise correlation among real generation-4 siblings runs from 0.544 to 1.000, with family means of 0.770, 0.837, 0.843, 0.897, 0.952 and 0.999, so this is not a low-correlation regime.

Over 100 draws for each of the 6 families, 600 draws in total, the mean of the family means is 0.599 against the analytic prediction of 0.600. The probability that a family with NO persistent skill differences at all is family-killed by the 0.50 line runs from 61 to 72 percent across the six. The probability that such a family passes the 0.20 line runs from 3 to 9 percent. A block-permutation variant that permutes labels in 21-day blocks, and so retains part of each sibling's own persistence, gives family means of 0.590 to 0.640 and a mean of approximately 0.62, confirming the result is not an artifact of destroying within-sibling autocorrelation.

WHERE GENERATION 4'S OBSERVED VALUES ACTUALLY SIT. Against its OWN permutation null, each observed value falls at the following percentile. symmetric_tstat_trend_ff, observed 0.689, 62nd percentile. symmetric_tstat_trend_voltarget, observed 0.803, 72nd percentile. short_only_fast_macross_high_n, observed 0.651, 50th percentile. symmetric_macross_stop_geometry, observed 0.761, 71st percentile. below_ma_short_regime_trend, observed 0.873, 83rd percentile. breakout_vol_state_filter, observed 0.030, 0th percentile. Not one family reaches the 90th percentile, let alone the 95th. The two families that carried the nine strategies this gate killed sit at the 62nd and 72nd percentile of what the same family produces with no skill differences whatsoever. Against a calibrated null, generation 4 shows no statistically significant evidence of overfitting in any family.

A SECOND DEFECT, INDEPENDENT OF PARITY: THE ESTIMATOR IS TOO DISPERSE FOR THE THRESHOLDS APPLIED TO IT. The standard deviation of a single family's pbo across the permutation draws is approximately 0.24 at n_configs 5, and the repository's own test suite already documents approximately 0.23 at n_configs 8 with s equal to 8, where it records that a third of seeds fall outside the interval 0.25 to 0.75 and that a single-seed assertion would therefore prove nothing about the estimator. The gate's entire pass band, from 0 to 0.20, is therefore narrower than one standard deviation of the quantity being thresholded. This is not a parity effect and would survive a parity fix untouched. It applies to the even-sized historical families as well, which means the write-free diagnostic reported in the protocol-v4 note, that pbo would have killed half the families ever registered, rests on single-draw estimates of a statistic with that dispersion. That diagnostic's kills are not disturbed by the parity finding, since those families were even, but neither are they established as significant, because no per-family null was computed for them.

WHAT THIS EVIDENCE DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It does not establish that the nine strategies killed on pbo had genuine edge. They may be overfit; the finding is that this gate at this family size could not have distinguished the two cases, and a corrected gate is as likely to bury them again as not. It does not establish where the thresholds belong, only that a fixed threshold is the wrong instrument for a statistic whose null moves with family size, family size parity, sibling correlation and series length. It does not establish that breakout_vol_state_filter at the 0th percentile is a good family: its siblings are 0.999 correlated, meaning the swept filter barely changed the strategy, so its low pbo reflects the persistence of a tiny difference in a degenerate family rather than a robust edge, and every one of its members had already died at the screen on trade count. The family-size sweep run alongside this, at n_configs 4, 5, 8, 12 and 25 on synthetic correlated series, returned 0.518, 0.563, 0.536, 0.486 and 0.516 with 50 draws each; n_configs 5 is the highest as predicted, but those gaps are under two standard errors and that sweep is reported as consistent with the parity result rather than as independent support for it. The parity result rests on the analytic derivation, which is exact, and on the 600-draw real-data null that reproduced it to three decimal places.

THE DIRECTION DECIDED, WHICH TAKES EFFECT FOR GENERATION 5 ONWARD AND IS NOT APPLIED TO ANY EXISTING VERDICT. Two changes, to be specified and built under their own pre-declared protocol note before any generation is judged under them. First, the boundary tie is to be counted as a half event, so that omega exactly equal to 0.5 contributes one half rather than one to the overfit count, which makes the estimator unbiased at every family size and removes the parity defect at its source. Second, and the substantive change, the fixed 0.20 and 0.50 lines are to be replaced by a test of the observed pbo against the family's OWN permutation null, computed by the procedure described above, so that the gate becomes a hypothesis test whose reference distribution is calibrated to that family's size, parity, correlation and length rather than assumed. The cost is roughly one hundred additional CSCV evaluations per family, about two minutes, which is negligible against what a generation already spends. Neither change is drafted here; this note records the evidence and the direction so that both are on this chain before the protocol that implements them, and long before any result it would affect exists.

RATCHET POSITION. The change foreshadowed here runs in the permissive direction, because families that protocol-v4 killed would not necessarily be killed under it. It is therefore treated as a LOOSENING and carries the full burden that the standing rule imposes on one, regardless of whether correcting a demonstrable bias would also be defensible as a repair. That burden is discharged by publishing this evidence now, before the successor protocol is written and before generation 5 exists. The generation-4 per-gate breakdown promised by the protocol-v4 note was published first and separately, at registry entry 2503, deliberately carrying no argument, so that the breakdown could not be read as having been shaped by the remedy that followed it.

gauntlet-protocol-v5: Supersedes v4 for all FUTURE verdicts. v1, v2, v3 and v4 verdicts stand. All 107 previously graveyarded strategies remain buried, which is terminal; the composition-fingerprint guard still blocks re-registration of any of them; the lifecycle state machine is UNCHANGED, no new transitions, nothing resurrected, no amendment to terminal states. The three strategies in quarantine keep their protocol-v3 verdicts under the quarantine-standard-asymmetry note. Pre-declared before any generation-5 specification exists and before any strategy has been evaluated under it.

THIS NOTE IS THE ARGUMENT HALF OF A RATCHET REQUIREMENT. The evidence half was chained first and separately, as pbo-validity-evidence at registry entry 2511, deliberately before this note existed so that the measurements could not have been shaped by the remedy they justify. The generation-4 per-gate breakdown that protocol-v4 promised was chained before that again, at entry 2503, carrying no argument at all for the same reason. A reader checking whether this pipeline reasoned backwards from a desired answer should read those two entries in that order before reading this one.

WHAT CHANGES: ONE GATE. Only the pbo gate is amended. sharpe_floor, oos_negative, edge_decay, mc_p05, p_ruin, cost_stress and plateau are retained from protocol-v4 verbatim, at the same thresholds, in the same FAIL_ORDER position. The deflated Sharpe is still computed, still recorded, and still gates nothing at this stage and ranks nothing. The screen is untouched: screen-protocol-v1 keeps its 2023-12-31 train fence and its floor of 40 trades and net above zero after costs. The recorded-not-gated numbers are untouched: Harvey-Liu haircut, purged walk-forward, regime split, each still carrying its window key. The declared divergence from the SOP on purged walk-forward survives unchanged.

WHY THE PBO GATE IS AMENDED, IN ONE PARAGRAPH. Protocol-v4 set a fixed pass line at 0.20 and a family-kill line at 0.50, both presupposing that a family whose siblings have no persistent skill differences scores about 0.5. That presupposition is false in this implementation at small odd family sizes, and is only approximately true anywhere. The CSCV code counts a split as overfit when omega is at most 0.5, where omega is the winner's out-of-sample rank over n_configs plus one. That is Bailey, Borwein and Lopez de Prado's own convention, and at the family sizes their work assumes the boundary case has vanishing measure. At small odd n the median rank lands exactly on the boundary and is swept into the overfit count, making the uniform-rank null n_configs plus one over twice n_configs. At a family of five that is 0.600, which is ABOVE protocol-v4's own family-kill line. Every one of the twelve sibling groups registered before generation 4 was even and carried a null of 0.500. Every one of generation 4's six groups was exactly five. The cause was internal to protocol-v4: its plateau gate requires a registered sibling on both sides of a candidate, making five contiguous values the narrowest useful sweep, so v4's plateau rule drove every family onto the one arm where v4's pbo estimator is biased past v4's own kill threshold.

AMENDMENT 1, THE BOUNDARY TIE COUNTS AS A HALF EVENT. A split whose omega is exactly 0.5 contributes one half rather than one to the overfit count. This makes the uniform-rank null exactly 0.500 at every family size, odd or even, and removes the parity defect at its source. Strictly this amendment is redundant for gating once amendment 3 is in force, because a calibrated null absorbs any fixed bias. It is adopted anyway because the pbo number is RECORDED on every verdict and read by people, and a recorded statistic whose meaning depends on the parity of a family size is a trap for a later reader who does not know to check.

AMENDMENT 2, THE GATE COUNTS DISTINCT CONFIGURATIONS, NOT REGISTERED SIBLINGS, AND FAILS CLOSED BELOW FOUR. The effective configuration count of a family is the number of DISTINCT train-window equity curves among its registered siblings. Siblings whose curves are byte-identical are the same configuration observed more than once: the swept axis did not bind between them, and PBO cannot measure whether selecting among them generalises, because there is nothing to select. Below four distinct configurations the gate does not return a lenient value, it FAILS with reason pbo_underpowered. This follows protocol-v4's own rule for the plateau gate, which fails a family with no swept dense axis rather than passing it vacuously, on the stated ground that a gate which passes on the absence of evidence is not a gate. The same reasoning binds here and in the same direction.

This is not hypothetical. Generation 4's breakout_vol_state_filter registered five siblings sweeping the volatility percentile across its full dense grid, and four of the five produced byte-identical train equity curves: the filter admitted the same seven trades at 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 and 0.9, and only 1.0 differed. Its measured pairwise sibling correlation was 0.999. It scored a pbo of 0.030, the lowest on the chain and the 0th percentile of its own null, and under a naive percentile test it would have been the one generation-4 family to PASS the gate. It should not. Its low score records that a tiny difference between near-identical siblings was persistent, not that a real edge survives selection. Left unhandled, this inverts the gate: the less a swept axis matters, the more robust the family appears.

AMENDMENT 3, THE FIXED THRESHOLDS ARE REPLACED BY A TEST AGAINST THE FAMILY'S OWN NULL. The 0.20 and 0.50 lines are withdrawn. In their place the observed pbo is compared to a null distribution computed for THAT family, by permutation: 200 draws, in each of which the sibling labels are randomly permuted within each day before the pbo is recomputed. Permuting labels within a day preserves that day's cross-section exactly, so the family's real return distribution, its real sibling correlation and the real common market factor all survive, and only PERSISTENT sibling-specific skill is destroyed. That is exactly the null the gate's semantics assume, and computing it per family calibrates the reference to that family's size, parity, correlation and series length rather than assuming values for all four.

The direction of the test is deliberate and is the opposite of v4's. A family PASSES only if its observed pbo falls at or below the 5th percentile of its own null, which is to say only if it DEMONSTRATES that selecting among its siblings generalises better than no skill would. It does not pass by failing to be convicted. A family whose observed pbo falls at or above the 95th percentile is killed entire, as under v4, with every member carrying the pbo_family_kill flag and each keeping its own first failure in FAIL_ORDER as its recorded reason. Anything between fails the configuration and leaves the family alive. Under v4 the burden ran the other way: a family passed unless its score exceeded a fixed line, so a gate with no power passed everything. Under v5 a gate with no power passes nothing, which is the correct direction for a gate standing between a backtest and capital.

THE GATE, STATED AS A PROCEDURE. First, compute the effective configuration count as the number of distinct train-window equity curves; if it is below four, fail pbo_underpowered. Second, compute the observed pbo by CSCV at S equals 16 over all 12870 splits, on the train window only, with every registered sibling in the matrix including screen deaths, and with the boundary tie counted as a half event. Third, compute the family's permutation null over 200 draws by the procedure above. Fourth, if the observed value is at or above the 95th percentile of that null, kill the family. Fifth, if it is at or below the 5th percentile, pass. Sixth, otherwise fail pbo. The train window remains the only window used: the 2024-onward holdout has been consumed three times and this protocol does not consume it a fourth.

WHAT THIS WOULD HAVE DONE TO GENERATION 4, STATED BECAUSE IT IS THE OBVIOUS TEST OF WHETHER THIS PROTOCOL WAS REASONED BACKWARDS. It would have produced ZERO SURVIVORS, exactly as v4 did. The nine strategies that v4 killed on pbo sit at the 62nd and 72nd percentile of their own family nulls, nowhere near the 5th, so they fail amendment 3. The one family that would have cleared the percentile test, breakout_vol_state_filter at the 0th, fails amendment 2 with an effective configuration count of two, and every one of its members had already died at the screen on trade count regardless. The nine sharpe_floor deaths and the one p_ruin death are unaffected, both gates preceding pbo in FAIL_ORDER. This protocol therefore does not resurrect a single generation-4 strategy and was not built to. What it changes is the REASON the generation returned zero, from a threshold that could not have distinguished an overfit family from a clean one at that family size, to a test that can.

COST. A permutation null is 200 additional CSCV evaluations per family. Measured on this machine over a 2327-day train window, one evaluation is about 0.9 seconds at five configurations and about 4.4 seconds at twenty-five, so a null costs about three minutes per five-configuration family and about fifteen minutes per twenty-five-configuration family, or roughly twenty minutes for a six-family generation of the shape generation 4 produced. This is the dominant cost of the gauntlet and it is accepted. It is embarrassingly parallel across draws and across families.

WHAT IS KNOWINGLY NOT FIXED, AND IS THE MOST LIKELY REASON THIS PROTOCOL WILL DISAPPOINT. The pbo estimator is DISPERSE, and amendment 3 calibrates its centre without narrowing it. Measured standard deviation of a single family's estimate is about 0.24 across the six real generation-4 families at five configurations, and in a synthetic sweep that holds everything else fixed it falls only from about 0.21 at five configurations to about 0.19 at twenty-five, so enlarging families buys much less than it appears to. A test demanding the 5th percentile of a distribution that wide is a demanding test, and it is entirely possible that no family this Composer produces will ever clear it. That would mean generation 5 and its successors return zero for a reason no better than the last one, and it is recorded here, before any generation-5 number exists, so that it cannot be discovered later and presented as a surprise. The honest position is that this protocol makes the gate INTERPRETABLE and does not make it POWERFUL, and that no evidence currently on this chain establishes that a real family can clear a calibrated pbo test at all.

RATCHET POSITION. This protocol contains a LOOSENING and is declared as one. Amendment 3 withdraws two fixed thresholds, and families that protocol-v4 would have killed will not necessarily be killed under it, so the permissive direction is real regardless of whether correcting a demonstrable bias would also be defensible as a repair. The standing rule requires the evidence and the argument on this chain before the results a loosening would affect exist. The evidence was chained at entry 2511 and the argument is this note, both before any generation-5 specification has been composed. Amendments 1 and 2 are tightenings and would have been permitted freely on their own. Nothing here is applied to any existing verdict, and the rule that keeps 107 strategies buried is untouched: they stay buried under the protocols that judged them, exactly as generations 1 through 3 did when v4 superseded their standards.

STATED BEFORE ANY RESULT EXISTS. A zero-survivor generation 5 is an acceptable outcome, for the same reason a zero-survivor generation 4 was. The pre-committed consequence carried over from protocol-v4 is carried over again and strengthened: if generation 5 produces no survivors, a per-gate breakdown will again be published on this chain before any threshold is discussed or any successor protocol is drafted, and for the pbo gate that breakdown will additionally report each family's effective configuration count and the full percentile of its observed value against its own null, so that the next reader can tell an underpowered family from a convicted one without rerunning anything.

pbo-power-evidence: EVIDENCE ONLY. It records what protocol-v5's PBO gate can detect and what generation 4's families actually offered it, and it proposes nothing. No threshold is changed, no gate is amended, no successor protocol is drafted here, and no verdict on this chain is disturbed. The protocol-v5 note chained at registry entry 2512 stands exactly as written; every strategy stays where it is. This is published for the same reason the generation-4 breakdown at entry 2503 and the validity evidence at entry 2511 were: so that when a change is eventually argued for, the measurements behind it are already on the record and cannot have been chosen to fit the conclusion.

WHY THIS WAS MEASURED. The protocol-v5 note names this as its own biggest weakness, in its own words: it is entirely possible that no family this Composer produces will ever clear the gate, and no evidence on this chain establishes that a real family can clear a calibrated PBO test at all. That is a question about the gate's POWER, and it is answerable without running a generation and without touching the holdout.

METHOD. Synthetic families are built to mirror the real ones: a common market factor taken from generation 4's symmetric_tstat_trend_ff, plus idiosyncratic noise at the residual standard deviation measured in that same family, giving a common-factor sd of 0.00472, an idiosyncratic sd of 0.00179 and a total of 0.00505. Into each family an edge is PLANTED: one configuration receives a persistent daily drift sized so that its annualized Sharpe advantage over its siblings equals a stated number, where a 1.0 advantage is 0.000264 of extra daily mean return. That is precisely the situation the gate exists to reward, a family in which selecting the in-sample best genuinely generalises. Each family is then judged exactly as protocol-v5 judges one: CSCV at S=16 over all 12870 splits on the train window with the boundary tie as a half event, compared against that family's own permutation null, passing at or below the 5th percentile. Five independent families per cell give a detection rate rather than a single draw. The diagnostic is diagnose_pbo_power.py, write-free by construction.

WHAT THE GATE DETECTS, at five configurations, five families per cell, fifty-draw nulls. At a planted advantage of 0.00 the observed PBO averaged 0.617 and sat at the 62nd percentile of its own null, detected 1 of 5. At 0.25, PBO 0.474 at the 47th percentile, detected 0 of 5. At 0.50, PBO 0.109 at the 6th percentile, detected 3 of 5. At 0.75, PBO 0.005 at the 0th percentile, detected 5 of 5. At 1.00 and at 2.00, detected 5 of 5. At twelve configurations a 0.50 advantage was detected 4 of 5 and a 1.00 advantage 5 of 5, so a larger family helps, modestly. The single detection at a planted advantage of ZERO is the gate's false-positive rate behaving as designed rather than a defect: at a true 5 percent level the chance of at least one pass in five trials is about 23 percent.

THE GATE IS THEREFORE NOT DECORATIVE. It was reasonable to fear, from the protocol-v5 note's own warning, that a test demanding the 5th percentile of a distribution with a standard deviation near 0.24 would forbid everything. It does not. A persistent advantage of 0.75 annualized Sharpe is detected every time and one of 0.50 most of the time. The gate rewards a real edge at an effect size that is large but not absurd.

WHAT GENERATION 4 ACTUALLY OFFERED IT. The quantity the gate must resolve is the winner's margin over its NEAREST RIVAL, not the family's best-worst spread, because the ranking that CSCV performs is decided at the top of the family. Measured on the committed train-window curves, those margins were: breakout_vol_state_filter 0.000, symmetric_tstat_trend_voltarget 0.010, below_ma_short_regime_trend 0.058, short_only_fast_macross_high_n 0.059, symmetric_tstat_trend_ff 0.097, symmetric_macross_stop_geometry 0.103. The corresponding best-worst spreads, which flatter the families and are recorded only for context, were 0.055, 0.364, 0.161, 0.212, 0.392 and 0.263. So the gate needs roughly 0.50 and the best real family supplied 0.103. The shortfall is a factor of five at its narrowest and unbounded at its widest, since one family's margin is exactly zero.

THE READING THIS FORCES. Generation 4's families did not fail the PBO gate because the gate was set too high. They failed because there was almost nothing to select between, and the gate said so correctly. When the best configuration in a family beats its nearest rival by one hundredth of a Sharpe point, choosing between them IS arbitrary, and a statistic asking whether that choice generalises is answering the question it was asked. No threshold could repair this without making the gate stop reporting a true thing.

AN OBSERVED TENSION BETWEEN TWO GATES, RECORDED WITHOUT A PROPOSED REMEDY. The plateau gate added by protocol-v4 rewards a FLAT neighbourhood: a candidate qualifies only if it and every one-step neighbour score at least 90 percent of the family best, on the stated reasoning that a lone peak surrounded by cliffs is the signature of overfitting rather than of edge. The PBO gate rewards a SEPARABLE one, because on a flat neighbourhood the in-sample winner is chosen by noise and does not persist out of sample. A dense sweep of one parameter is flat by construction, which is what the dense block types were introduced to guarantee. These two gates were adopted in successive protocols and, on the object they are both applied to, they pull in opposite directions. It is not a strict contradiction: a family holding a plateau of genuinely distinct good configurations alongside genuinely worse ones would satisfy both, since the in-sample winner would come from the plateau and still outrank the poor members out of sample. Generation 4 produced no family of that shape, and nothing in the Composer's instructions asks for one. This is recorded as an observation about the gate stack, not as an argument for changing either gate.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It is a LOWER BOUND on what the gate demands, not an estimate: the planted edge is uniform and persistent, the most detectable shape an edge can take, so a regime-dependent or episodic edge of the same average size would need to be larger still. Five repeats per cell fixes the shape of the detection curve but not its exact rates, and a fifty-draw null resolves the 5th percentile coarsely. It does not establish that no family this Composer could ever build reaches a 0.50 margin, only that none of generation 4's six came within a factor of five. It does not establish anything about the plateau gate's own thresholds, which have still never fired on real data. And it is not evidence that any particular strategy on this chain was wrongly buried: the nine strategies that died at the PBO gate in generation 4 sat at the 62nd and 72nd percentile of their own nulls, and nothing measured here moves them.

RATCHET POSITION. This note changes nothing and therefore carries no ratchet burden of its own. It is filed in advance of any argument that might cite it, so that a later proposal to move a threshold, to redefine what a sibling group is, or to change what the PBO gate is computed over, must be argued against measurements that already existed before the proposal did.

gauntlet-protocol-v6: Supersedes v5 for all FUTURE verdicts. v1, v2, v3, v4 and v5 verdicts stand. All 107 previously graveyarded strategies remain buried, which is terminal, and that expressly includes the 7 buried as sibling_not_selected under protocol-v3, which this protocol would not bury today; the composition-fingerprint guard still blocks re-registration of any of them; the three strategies in quarantine keep their protocol-v3 verdicts under the quarantine-standard-asymmetry note. Pre-declared before any generation-5 specification exists and before any strategy has been evaluated under it.

THE PRINCIPLE THIS PROTOCOL ENCODES, stated by Coen on 2026-08-21: each individual edge needs to be tested, regardless of how similar it is to another, and EVERY INDIVIDUAL EDGE MUST BE STANDALONE WHEN RUNNING THROUGH THE GAUNTLET. A configuration is a candidate in its own right. It is judged on its own evidence, and its resemblance to a sibling is not evidence about it. Three mechanisms in v4 and v5 decided a strategy's fate on something other than its own performance, and this protocol removes all three from the gate battery while keeping every one of them as a recorded number.

STANDALONE IS A CHECKABLE PROPERTY, NOT AN ASPIRATION, AND IT IS THE INVARIANT THIS PROTOCOL IS ACCOUNTABLE TO. After the three removals below, every input to every remaining gate is a property of the strategy alone: its own in-sample and out-of-sample trades, its own daily returns, its own train-window Sharpe, and its own trades re-run under doubled slippage. No gate reads a sibling, a group, a neighbour, a grid position or a family statistic. One group-level quantity survives in the recorded metrics, sibling_group_n, and it is worth stating that it was never read by a gate even under v4 and v5; it is provenance, not judgment. A future amendment that reintroduces any group-level input to the battery contradicts this protocol's founding principle and needs its own pre-declared note saying so in those terms.

CHANGE 1, SELECTION IS RETIRED. Under v3 the gauntlet promoted the single highest deflated Sharpe per sibling group; under v4 and v5 it promoted the single strongest neighbourhood floor. Under v6 every strategy that passes the gate battery proceeds to quarantine. select_survivors no longer selects, the sibling_not_selected transition is retired for future runs, and a sibling group ceases to be a competition. The cost of the retired rule is measurable rather than hypothetical: 7 strategies passed every gate on their own evidence and were graveyarded because a similar sibling scored higher, all of them in generation 3, which produced 10 gauntlet passers and quarantined 3.

CHANGE 2, THE PBO GATE BECOMES A RECORDED NUMBER. CSCV is still computed exactly as protocol-v5 computes it, with the boundary tie as a half event, over distinct configurations, against the family's own permutation null, and the observed value, the null percentiles, the distinct count and the draw count are all still written to every verdict. It no longer gates. pbo and pbo_underpowered leave FAIL_ORDER, and the family kill is retired. Two reasons, both already on this chain. First, PBO is a statement about a SELECTION PROCEDURE applied to a family, not about whether one configuration's edge is real, so under the principle above it cannot bury a configuration that passed its own gates. Second, the power evidence chained at registry entry 2513 measured what it can resolve: a planted advantage of 0.75 annualized Sharpe over siblings is detected every time and 0.50 most of the time, while the winner's margin over its nearest rival in generation 4's six families was 0.000, 0.010, 0.058, 0.059, 0.097 and 0.103. A gate that needs roughly 0.50 and is handed 0.10 at best is not resolving the thing it is being asked to decide. It should report, and this protocol has it report.

CHANGE 3, THE PLATEAU GATE BECOMES A RECORDED NUMBER. Neighbourhood qualification is still computed and the outcome still recorded, but it no longer gates and no longer selects. This is the change that sits least comfortably, and it is stated plainly rather than smoothed over: the plateau rule was adopted from the trading-systems SOP, whose Phase 4 forbids selecting the best single configuration and requires selection by neighbourhood quality, and it was ratified by Coen on 2026-08-18 with its both-sides neighbour requirement accepted deliberately. v6 does not claim the SOP is wrong. It observes that the plateau rule judges a candidate by its NEIGHBOURS' scores and by its position on a grid, which the principle above does not permit, and that with selection itself retired by change 1 there is no longer a slot for the rule to allocate. THIS IS A DECLARED DIVERGENCE FROM THE SOP, larger than the purged-walk-forward divergence v4 declared, and it means a research-layer candidate and a trading-systems candidate no longer face the same named standard. Protocol-v4 existed to make those two standards identical. That reconciliation is hereby partially undone, deliberately, and any claim that both pipelines clear one bar must stop being made until it is repaired.

GATES RETAINED, UNCHANGED, IN THIS ORDER: sharpe_floor at 0.4 on the train window, oos_negative, edge_decay above minus 25 percent on volatility-normalized per-trade edge, mc_p05 above 1.0, p_ruin below 0.05, cost_stress positive at double slippage. Six gates, every one of them a property of the individual strategy and computable without reference to any sibling. That is the whole battery under v6. The screen is untouched: screen-protocol-v1 keeps its 2023-12-31 train fence and its floor of 40 trades and net above zero after costs. Harvey-Liu haircut, purged walk-forward and the regime split remain recorded and not gating, each still carrying its window key.

WHY THIS COSTS NOTHING STATISTICALLY, WHICH IS THE LEAST OBVIOUS PART. Promoting every passer rather than one looks like it should inflate the multiple-testing burden. It does not, because the trials denominator has never counted promotions. registered_n is len(all_specs) and trials_n is the effective-trials clustering over every registered strategy including every buried one; generation 4's verdicts record trials_n of 2 clusters over registered_n of 110. Promoting five siblings instead of one leaves both numbers exactly where they were and leaves the deflated Sharpe unchanged. The one-winner-per-group rule was therefore never carrying the multiple-testing load that its presence implied. It was a capacity decision about how many strategies enter forward testing, presented as a statistical one, and this protocol stops presenting it that way.

WHERE MULTIPLICITY IS NOW PRICED, AND THE RISK THAT CREATES. The deflated Sharpe at 0.95 remains the quarantine-to-live gate, computed on the forward record with N over all registrations, exactly as protocol-v3 placed it. After v6 that is the ONLY place the search burden is priced. That gate has never been calibrated and cannot bind for 60 trading days, and it is now load-bearing in a way it was not before. This protocol loosens the gauntlet while the gate downstream of it remains uncalibrated. That is recorded here, before any result, as the principal risk v6 takes on.

STATED BEFORE ANY RESULT EXISTS, AND THIS IS THE PART A LATER READER SHOULD HOLD THIS CHAIN TO. Removing three rejection mechanisms will produce MORE survivors. A generation returning ten or twenty quarantine entries is now plausible where v5 returned none, and generation 3 would have returned 10 rather than 3. THAT WOULD NOT BE EVIDENCE OF EDGE. It would be evidence of a looser gate, and it must not be reported, presented, or sold as a breakthrough. The honest description of a v6 generation that produces survivors is that a protocol which previously discarded them stopped doing so. The forward record in quarantine is what can distinguish the two, and only after it exists.

WHAT IS KNOWINGLY GIVEN UP. v4 and v5 added five rejection mechanisms between them and v6 keeps one of them, the Sharpe floor. The gauntlet's discriminating power now rests entirely on six per-strategy gates, and generation 4 demonstrated that a family with no selectable internal structure whatsoever can pass all six: the nine strategies that died at v4's PBO gate had cleared every one of them. Under v6 those nine would have reached quarantine. Whether that is right depends entirely on whether their forward records justify it, which is precisely the question quarantine exists to answer and precisely the question no gauntlet gate can answer in advance.

RATCHET POSITION. This protocol is a LOOSENING and is declared as one without qualification. Three rejection mechanisms are removed, none is added, and no threshold is tightened anywhere to compensate. The standing rule requires the evidence and the argument on this chain before the results a loosening would affect exist. The evidence was chained first and separately: the generation-4 per-gate breakdown at entry 2503, the PBO validity evidence at entry 2511, and the PBO power evidence at entry 2513, the last of which measured the gate's resolution against the separation real families actually exhibit. This note is the argument, and it exists before any generation-5 specification has been composed. Nothing here is applied to any existing verdict, and the rule keeping 107 strategies buried is untouched, including the 7 this protocol would not bury today. That asymmetry is the same one the quarantine-standard-asymmetry note declared for a different set of strategies, and it is accepted here for the same reason: re-judging closed verdicts under a later standard is the failure mode this whole chain exists to prevent, and it does not become acceptable when the later standard is kinder.
